SELECT
  tm.title AS macro_title,
  tm.usage_count AS current_usage_count,
  COALESCE(ch.event_count, 0) AS logged_update_event_count,
  ch.sum_increment AS sum_of_logged_increments,
  ch.first_update_at AS first_logged_update_at,
  ch.last_update_at AS last_logged_update_at,
  tm.created_at AS macro_created_at
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, usage_count, created_at
  FROM macros
  ORDER BY usage_count DESC, id
  LIMIT 5
) tm
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    entity_id,
    COUNT(*) AS event_count,
    SUM((after_data->>'usage_count')::numeric - (before_data->>'usage_count')::numeric) AS sum_increment,
    MIN(occurred_at) AS first_update_at,
    MAX(occurred_at) AS last_update_at
  FROM change_history
  WHERE entity_table = 'macros'
    AND 'usage_count' = ANY(changed_columns)
  GROUP BY entity_id
) ch ON ch.entity_id = tm.id
ORDER BY tm.usage_count DESC, tm.id
note: We don't have last week's report output stored to match macro ids against, so the 5 macros here are today's top 5 by macros.usage_count (tie-broken by id) rather than a literal re-identification of last week's rows — flag if that set needs to match exactly, we'd need the prior report's macro ids. Also note change_history is only filtered by entity_table='macros' and changed_columns containing 'usage_count' (no entity_schema filter was specified/available), and per-macro figures are null for logged_update_event_count fields if no matching change_history rows exist.
